## Rule (decoded from ARC-GEN generator `7447852a`, verified)

`height` is ALWAYS 3; `width` W in [5,25]. The output is a **period-12 column tile** of a
fixed 3x12 base, cropped to width W (cols >= W are all-zero padding). It is **purely
positional / input-INDEPENDENT modulo width**. Base block (color indices):
```
2 0 0 0 2 4 4 4 2 0 0 0
4 2 0 2 0 2 4 2 0 2 0 2
4 4 2 0 0 0 2 0 0 0 2 4
```
The output one-hot has THREE active channels: **ch0** (background color-0 inside the grid),
**ch2** (red zigzag == input ch2), **ch4** (yellow fill). The generator's mode cycle (period 6
over zigzag peaks/troughs) makes the column period 12 = the red zigzag period 4 LCM the fills.
Verified: period-12 tile cropped to W matches 25/25 officials and 200000/200000 generator pairs.

**ch0 is mandatory** — `convert_to_numpy` encodes color-0 cells as ch0=1 and `verify_subset`
compares the full [1,10,30,30] one-hot (13 ch0 ones in a W=10 case). Padding cells (rows>=3 or
cols>=W) are all-channels-zero (color "no color" sentinel 10), NOT ch0=1.

## Algorithm sketch (current 226 staged candidate)

Team-best anchor was Aditya's one-node signed free-output Einsum:
```
out[b,o,h,w] = sum_{c,k} input[b,c,h,w] * source[c,k] * target[o,k] * row[k,h] * col[k,w]
einsum: 'bchw,ck,ok,kh,kw->bohw'
```
The graph has zero charged intermediates (#89/#109/#119): `input` and `output` are exempt and the
rank-3 products are in-kernel. Charged tensors are exactly:
- `source[10,3]` = 30 params
- `target[10,3]` = 30 params
- `row[3,30]` = 90 params
- `col[3,30]` = 90 params

Total static/profile cost is **240**. The older rank-6 `ChanSel/RowSel/U/V` sketch remains useful
history, but its 354 "hard floor" was disproven by this signed rank-3 formulation.

Worker-176c staged a sub-240 channel-bank factorization that is algebraically byte-equal to the
240 anchor while staying in the same terminal free-output Einsum:
```
out[b,o,h,w] = sum_{c,g,k} input[b,c,h,w] * source2[c,g] * target2[o,g] * mix[g,k] * row[k,h] * col[k,w]
einsum: 'bchw,cg,og,gk,kh,kw->bohw'
```
It keeps `row[3,30]` and `col[3,30]` unchanged, and replaces the duplicated channel columns for
`k=0,1` with `source2[10,2]`, `target2[10,2]`, and `mix[2,3]`. Charged params are exactly
20 + 20 + 6 + 90 + 90 = **226**, memory 0, one node named `output`.

## Don't-do log

- **Don't store the template as params/canvas** (LIVE's 2x[1,1,3,30]=180 + the [1,10,3,30] Concat
  1800B). The output is positional; a free-output einsum factors it for ~10x less.
- **Don't materialize any [1,10,*,*] or [1,1,30,30] tensor.** Make the einsum output `[1,10,30,30]`
  directly (named `output`, exempt). Any intermediate channel/canvas tensor charges 900-1800B and
  blows the cost past 450.
- **Don't add a separate width-reduction** (`ReduceMax/Sum(input)` -> [1,30] F32 = 120B). Contract
  the input's channel axis INSIDE the einsum (in-kernel, #89) -> active mask is free.
- **Don't cast the input to F16** for the einsum — casting the full [1,10,30,30] frame creates an
  18000B intermediate. Keep all factors F32 so the free input feeds directly (no cast node).
- **Don't try red-passthrough + bg-as-complement** (ch0 = A - ch2 - ch4): it needs ADDITIVE terms
  mixing input-derived and basis-derived contributions -> two einsums + Add materializes the
  [1,10,30,30] canvas. The unified multiplicative einsum (all 3 colors in ColTile) is the way.
- **Don't reach for Pad(wrap) column tiling as a runtime node** (540B [3,3,30] intermediate) or a
  PhaseMap[12,30] one-hot (360 params) — storing the tiled ColTile directly (270, or 234 rank-6)
  is cheaper than base+tiling either way.

## Conditional sub-240 audit (Worker-176b, 2026-06-22)

No global hard floor is claimed. The reviewer-requested attacks were exhausted as follows:

- **Fixed-pattern active-mask Einsum without `source`** (`bchw,ok,kh,kw->bohw`, cost 210 if k=3):
  exact-fails. The flattened binary pattern matrix `[(output_color,row)=30, col=25]` has rank 6,
  so a k=3 exact fixed-pattern representation is impossible.
- **Grouped Conv under 240**: audited legal same-shape Conv groups with bias/no-bias and full useful
  dilation/pad splits. `group=2, area<=4` enumerated 433,922 cases; every case had an exact
  contradictory feature certificate before LP solving. `group=5, area<=11` and `group=10, area<=22`
  fail by channel partition: output ch4 cannot read input ch0/ch2, while task176 inputs only use
  ch0/ch2; ch4 is bias-only and spatially constant.
- **Channel-factor shrink**: source-omitted is the rank-6 failure above; target-omitted has no
  output-channel label and cannot create ch4; tied/shared selectors need an additional asymmetric
  remap or the second selector bank, returning to >=240; sparse active-channel remaps are not legal
  cheap operands and Slice/Gather remaps create charged F32 predecessors (#109/#119).
- **Row shrink under #132 growth-op law**: `row[3,3]` is shape-invalid in the terminal Einsum because
  label `h` spans the 30-high input/output axis. Padding a small row factor charges a `[3,30]` F32
  intermediate = 360 bytes; emitting `[1,10,3,30]` then padding to output charges 3,600 bytes. The
  possible 81-param save cannot pay.
- **Col shrink / period-12 bank**: current `col[:,0:25]` rank is 3. Exact factorization
  `A[3,3]+B[3,30]` costs 99, worse than dense `col[3,30]=90`; k<3 fails. A `[3,12]` period bank
  needs either a same-node `phase[12,30]` map (360 params) or a runtime-grown `[3,30]` F32
  predecessor (360 bytes), both worse than 90.

**Superseded conclusion:** the no-`<240` result was conditional on the attacks tried in Worker-176b.
Worker-176c found the missed `source/target` duplicate-column role split requested by review:

and is byte-equal to the 240 anchor.
